entry_point: PSR-7 library API: the URI string constructor, the host component setter, the parse_url-parts constructor, building and re-targeting a request from any UriInterface implementation, changing a request's URI, parsing an absolute-form request message, serializing a request, populating a request from server globals, and the injected authority constructor and Host-header helper

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit: a host carrying user information, a path, a query, a fragment, a backslash, an embedded port or a bracket fragment is accepted by the component setter and the parts constructor, and reaches the generated Host header from a foreign UriInterface through Request construction and URI replacement, through Utils::modifyRequest (URI change and missing-Host fallback), through Message::toString, through the injected Uri::withAuthority and Utils::hostHeaderFor, and through the string parser for bracketed and backslash forms; ServerRequest::getUriFromGlobals passes SERVER_NAME to the host setter unparsed. Every security test fails on the pinned (injected) tree and passes on the reference fix.
sites: src/Uri.php:104 the bracketed-literal fast path of the parser (published fix far site)
src/Uri.php:445-460 Uri::assertValidHost, the shared host validator strengthened by the published fix
src/Request.php:146-160 generated Host header from an arbitrary UriInterface (published fix far site, validated through the shared validator)
src/ServerRequest.php:265-268 SERVER_NAME/SERVER_ADDR fallback into the host setter
src/Utils.php:211-233 Utils::modifyRequest copies a foreign URI host into the Host header (pattern B)
src/Message.php:24-26 Message::toString writes the URI host raw when there is no Host header (pattern B)
src/Uri.php withAuthority (injected sibling: authority split with a direct host assignment)
src/Utils.php hostHeaderFor (injected sibling: Host-header formatting from any UriInterface)
routes: T1: component setter, parts constructor, string parser, foreign-URI request construction and re-targeting, absolute-form message parsing and the server-name fallback, with user information, path, query, fragment, backslash, port colon and bracket shapes
T2: request-modification helper, URI-change branch and missing-Host fallback
T3: request serialization without a Host header, using a request supplied by another implementation
T5 (injected): Host-header formatting helper from any UriInterface
verified.services: none; PHPUnit runs offline against the installed vendor tree
verified.project_tests_run: tests/UriTest.php, tests/RequestTest.php, tests/ServerRequestTest.php, tests/MessageTest.php, tests/UtilsTest.php — 181 tests / 455 assertions pass on the pinned (injected) tree, on the reference fix and on every check patch; the hidden suites add 61 security and 48 functional tests.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: every route records or derives the very host it is given; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource whose check could be substituted.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the protected value is one host string with no peer, role or direction dimension.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every route both reads and records or emits the host; there is no separate read-only view to guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the port is appended only after the host is taken, and a numeric port cannot introduce a delimiter into the host component.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the protected value is a single host string; the delimiter, colon and bracket rules cover malformed spellings directly, with no identity fields to parse.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: validation is over the supplied string alone; no external lookup can return nothing and make the check fail open.

traps.shape: the host well-formedness rule itself: a delimiter list that omits the backslash, a bare port colon outside brackets, and bracket first/last balance, reached through the component setter, the parts constructor, the string parser, a request built or re-targeted from a foreign URI implementation, an absolute-form message target and the server-name fallback; coupled with bracketed values whose contents are not a valid IP address, zone identifiers and internationalized names that must keep being accepted
traps.where: src/Uri.php:104 and src/Uri.php:445-460 (consumed by src/Request.php:146-160, src/ServerRequest.php:265-268 and src/Message.php:306-334)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported value is one user-information spelling, so a delimiter-only regex looks complete; a backslash is not an RFC 3986 authority delimiter, a colon in a host looks like a harmless port, and the library's own stricter Host-header validator looks authoritative but rejects bracketed values that must keep working
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-C2W2-PRH8-QM98) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the request-modification helper copies a host from a foreign URI implementation into the Host header, both when a new URI is supplied and when a missing Host header is filled from the request URI
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the fallback comment says it merely matches Request::__construct(), and the copied value passes the generic header-value check, so the host reads as already validated and owned by the URI implementation
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; upstream 3.2 added the same validator calls to both branches

traps.shape: request serialization writes the URI host into a Host line when the message has no Host header, including for a request object supplied by another implementation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a serialization/debug helper whose branch looks unreachable because the library's own requests always carry a Host header; another implementation's request is assumed to have validated itself
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; upstream 3.2 added the same validator call there

traps.shape: an authority constructor splits user information and port from the supplied authority and records the remainder as the host without validating it; path, query, fragment, backslash, double-port and bracket shapes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the method receives a complete authority and already separates the delimiters it knows, so the remaining text reads as the host and needs no further check
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling written in the style of the surrounding URI component helpers, as the public counterpart to the authority getter

traps.shape: a Host-header formatting helper returns host plus port for any URI implementation without validating the host
traps.where: src/Utils.php hostHeaderFor (injected next to the request-modification helper)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the URI implementation is expected to have validated its own host, and the helper only appends a numeric port
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling; a plausible convenience that formats the same host-plus-port value the request helper builds
